mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate component of equity discount rates, increasing present values of future cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through continuous valuation effects.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 8.0% for three consecutive months signals severe labor market distress, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative equity returns as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 8.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based consumer demand contraction, causing negative equity returns through reduced corporate revenue visibility and increased recession risk.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases (SPX 20-day returns positive in >40% of triggered instances).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 95.0 (2017=100) indicates a supply shock reducing corporate output capacity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as profit margins compress and earnings forecasts decline.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO < 95.0 or the effect reverses during high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%).

mechanism_narrative: Strong real GDP growth (GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through sustained profit momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting aggressive monetary tightening that increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate accelerating labor market deterioration, triggering negative equity returns through reduced consumer spending and earnings downgrades.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining PAYEMS and rising UNRATE fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases (SPX 20-day returns positive in >40% of triggered instances).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 600.0 thousand units signal a housing market recovery, boosting consumer confidence and retail spending, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days through improved corporate revenue visibility.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when HOUST exceeds 600.0 thousand units or the effect is absent during recessions (GDPC1 growth < 0.0%).
